title: A ledger fault in one relay delivery abandons the other deliveries and skips backoff
body:
## Summary
relay_finished returns on the first non-Conflict ledger error, so later deliveries in the same pass are neither staged nor acknowledged, the inbox pass is skipped and no backoff is set.

## Description
crates/table-runtime/src/relay.rs:111 (`Err(e) => return app(Err(e))` inside the batch loop) and crates/table-runtime/src/relay.rs:122 (acknowledge_relay `?`) exit relay_finished before the remaining deliveries, before consume_inbox (crates/table-runtime/src/relay.rs:125) and before the failure backoff. A Conflict is already handled per deal ("One deal's refusal stops that deal only"); any other fault on one deal stops every deal in the pass, and the next tick retries at once with no wait. Fixed: collect the first fault, keep processing the other deliveries, run the inbox pass, count the pass as failed for backoff, then return the fault.

## Flow
- start_relay sends up to 4 routes; their deliveries come back as one RelayFinished message
- delivery 1's stage_relay_batch fails with a non-Conflict ledger error
- delivery 2's batches and acknowledgements are dropped (its sent messages are re-sent next pass); relay_retry_at stays 0

## Expected impact
Wallets with one bad route stop re-sending other routes' messages and stop hot-looping the relay on a persistent fault. Could break: a DB-wide fault does a little more work per pass before surfacing.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - one deal's ledger fault no longer drops the other deals' delivery bookkeeping
Before: walked: 2 deliveries, the first faults -> acks recorded for the second 0, relay_failures 0, inbox pass skipped
After: predicted: acks for the second 1, relay_failures 1, inbox pass run, the error still returned
Method: simulation - nothing in-tree makes stage_relay_batch fail with a non-Conflict error without a fault-injecting ledger; three cases walked (Conflict, fault on the first delivery, fault on the last)
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: relay_tests: Delivery::for_test for a deal whose staging faults (a fault-injecting or closed ledger) followed by a valid delivery; assert the second delivery's relay_delivered rows, relay_failures == 1 and that the inbox pass ran

title: Market-watch planning swallows every per-deal error, so a fault stops checks silently
body:
## Summary
plan_market_watch keeps only Ok(Some(job)) from plan_one; ledger faults and an unreadable agent key end every price check with no Fault event and no trace.

## Description
crates/table-runtime/src/market_watch.rs:49 `if let Ok(Some(job)) = self.plan_one(...)` discards Err. plan_one returns Err for ledger faults (preference, has_open_operation, deal_category, reserve_market_check other than Conflict) and for select_signer when the agent key cannot be read (crates/table-runtime/src/market_watch.rs:132). The module doc (crates/table-runtime/src/market_watch.rs:35) says fail closed, which is right, but a fault leaves nothing behind: the tick reports Ok, OwnerFacts shows used_today unchanged, and the shield keeps holding deals for want of a fresh price. Fixed: keep failing closed per deal, but return the first error after the loop together with the planned jobs, so start_market_watch still spawns what was reserved (market_watch_busy is never leaked) and then surfaces the fault.

## Flow
- the keychain stops answering for agent.negotiator, or the ledger faults
- every watched due deal returns Err from plan_one; plan_market_watch returns Ok(vec![])
- no WalletEvent::Fault; watched seller deals sit in Agreed with a stale or missing price

## Expected impact
The owner can see why price checks stopped instead of an unexplained hold. Could break: a naive `?` in start_market_watch would leak market_watch_busy for jobs already reserved.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a fault that stops automatic price checks leaves a trace
Before: walked: vault denying agent.negotiator, 1 watched due deal -> jobs 0, plan result Ok, faults 0
After: predicted: jobs 0, plan result Err(Agent key unavailable) once per pass, no busy flag leaked
Method: simulation - the fix changes plan_market_watch's return shape and start_market_watch's error flow (M, risk 4); three cases walked (policy refusal stays silent, ledger fault surfaces, mixed pass still spawns the good job)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: market_watch_tests: the AgentKeyGone vault (crates/table-runtime/src/house_tests.rs) over one watched due deal plus one healthy deal on another runtime path; assert the error surfaces, the healthy job is still returned, and market_watch_busy holds only spawned jobs

title: A relay delivery task that panics is dropped with no failure, backoff or trace
body:
## Summary
start_relay keeps only Ok results from its JoinSet; a delivery task that panics vanishes, so the pass reads as clean and the backoff is reset.

## Description
crates/table-runtime/src/relay.rs:79 `if let Ok(result) = result { deliveries.push(result) }` drops a JoinError. relay_finished then sees fewer deliveries with failure=false (crates/table-runtime/src/relay.rs:93) and resets relay_failures and relay_retry_at (crates/table-runtime/src/relay.rs:134). A RelayApi implementation that panics on one route is retried every tick with no backoff and no Fault. Fixed: count a JoinError as a failed delivery for the pass.

## Flow
- a RelayApi::poll implementation panics for one route
- the JoinSet yields Err(JoinError), which is skipped
- relay_finished reports Ok and clears the backoff; the route is retried next tick, indefinitely

## Expected impact
The relay loop backs off instead of spinning on a crashing route, and the operator gets a Fault. Could break: nothing on the success path.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a crashed delivery counts as a failed pass
Before: walked: one panicking route -> relay_failures 0, Fault events 0
After: predicted: relay_failures 1, one Fault (Unavailable, relay delivery will retry)
Method: simulation - needs a spawned actor with a panicking RelayApi double and a wait on RelayFinished; not built this round
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: relay_tests: spawn a runtime with a RelayApi whose poll panics; after one relay pass assert relay_failures == 1 or a WalletEvent::Fault, red before

title: No test pins deliver()'s partial-send path: acks for the sent prefix, then the poll
body:
## Summary
When a send fails mid-way, deliver records acknowledgements only for the messages already sent and still polls; no test exercises it.

## Description
crates/table-runtime/src/relay.rs:212-218: on the first failed api.send the loop breaks with failed=true, keeping acks for the prefix, and the follow-up poll still runs. Every relay double in table-runtime tests either succeeds every send (InProcessRelay, crates/table-runtime/src/relay_tests.rs:298), fails every send (WakeRelay, RouterRelay and PendingHouseRelay in crates/table-runtime/src/house_tests.rs) or never answers (PendingRelay, crates/table-runtime/src/relay_tests.rs:161). A mutant that pushes the ack before the send, or drops the break, is expected to survive. Fixed: a relay double that fails the Nth send, driven through start_relay.

## Flow
- a route has 3 outgoing messages
- send 2 fails
- acks must be recorded for message 1 only; the pass counts as failed; the poll batch is still staged

## Expected impact
Protects the at-least-once delivery bookkeeping from a silent regression. Could break: nothing (test only).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - surviving mutants on the partial-send path
Before: mutation probe owed: ack-before-send and drop-break mutants expected to survive the current suite
After: predicted: both mutants red under the new test
Method: simulation - needs an actor-driven start_relay harness with a counting relay double, since deliver() is private to crate::relay
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: relay_tests: FailNthSend relay double over InProcessRelay, start_relay through a spawned actor; assert one relay_delivered row for a 3-message route whose second send fails; seed the ack-before-send mutant red

title: Agent public keys are re-derived from keychain secrets on read-only paths
body:
## Summary
seat_pair, house_offer and mandate_list (via market_watch_facts) read agent SECRET keys from the keychain only to take their public keys.

## Description
crates/table-runtime/src/pairing.rs:137-139 (seat_pair) and crates/table-runtime/src/pairing.rs:466-468 (house_offer) read agent.negotiator only for verifying_key(); market_watch_facts (crates/table-runtime/src/market_watch.rs:288) calls mandate_list, which reads all 3 agent secrets per call (crates/table-runtime/src/configuration.rs:199) to map a mandate's agent_key to its slot. The wallet already holds the owner public key in memory (713add0; af842c2 this round); the agent public keys are fixed at boot and could be held the same way. Signing sites keep reading the secret.

## Flow
- owner facts are read, or a pairing join runs
- each reads 1-3 agent secrets from the OS keychain
- the secret is used only for its public key

## Expected impact
Fewer keychain reads on owner-facts polls and pairing. Could break: a key rotation path would have to refresh the cached public keys.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - keychain reads on read-only paths
Before: measured this round with the recording vault: one watch pass over 3 deals plus 3 landed answers reads agent.negotiator 6 times (select_signer); owner_facts reads 3 agent entries per call
After: predicted: 0 agent-secret reads on seat_pair, house_offer and mandate_list
Method: probe - counts taken with the Recording vault in crates/table-runtime/src/market_watch_tests.rs; the change crosses service.rs and configuration.rs (another context), so it was not built here
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: the Recording vault in crates/table-runtime/src/market_watch_tests.rs: count agent.* reads across owner_facts() and a pairing join, before vs after caching agent public keys at Runtime::new

title: Owner market refresh checks the market key before the call, as the watch does
body:
## Summary
Candidate: market_refresh does not check that a market key is stored before calling the market service, unlike plan_one.

## Description
plan_one checks the channel3 entry before a fetch (crates/table-runtime/src/market_watch.rs:127); market_refresh (crates/table-runtime/src/market.rs:108-145) does not. Rejected: the real table_market client loads the key first and fails Unavailable before any HTTP (crates/table-market/src/lib.rs:76), and the client renders refusals by code, never the wallet's message (apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/priceCheck.test.tsx:41-49).

## Flow
- owner clicks Price check with no market key stored
- table_market loads the key, gets Unavailable, makes no HTTP call

## Expected impact
None measurable.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - an unconfigured market reads differently from an outage
Before: HTTP calls without a key 0; text shown refusalText(UNAVAILABLE)
After: HTTP calls 0; text shown refusalText(UNAVAILABLE)
Method: probe - read the client's key-load order and the UI's refusal mapping
Result: not-better
Gate: none
